$comment: Ground truth for retrieval, over the three CC-BY fixtures in
tests/fixtures/papers/. Written by READING the papers and recording what
each one says where -- not by running a retriever and keeping what it
found. A ground truth produced that way can only prove the index is
deterministic, which is not the claim the work order makes.
`expect` is the set of CORRECT answers, not one correct answer. Several
phrases legitimately occur on several pages, and pinning a single page
would make the set fail for being right. A query with an empty `expect`
must retrieve nothing, which is ADR-0004 A6 (a genuine absence) and A12
(a fabricated source must not be findable).
Matching is whitespace-insensitive, and that is a property of the corpus
rather than a convenience. ADR-0008 measured space glyphs at 0.03%-1.08%
across these papers: they space words by positioning, so extracted body
text arrives with words run together ('Dijkstra'salgorithmis'). A set
written with spaces would therefore describe text no query can match. The
one exception is recorded below rather than smoothed over.
The scope of this set is what it is: three papers, all single-column,
70 pages, no two-column material. It can say a query finds the right
excerpt. It cannot say the index handles a layout the corpus does not
contain.

arx-2610.09396.pdf.title: ARCS: Towards Precise Text-to-SQL via Structured Disambiguation

arx-2610.10596.pdf.title: Dijkstra Is NOT Greedy: A Global-to-Local Proof of Correctness

arx-2610.12393.pdf.title: HRIL: Learning Multimodal Synergy via Higher-Order Tensor Modeling

queries.why: The author's affiliation, on the title page. Unique in the corpus: no other paper is authored from that institution, so a retriever that also returned the other two papers would be answering a different question.
A sentence about prior work (Sniedovich), not the paper's own claim. It appears once, in the space-separated paper, so it is also the case that proves the retriever handles normally-spaced text.
Section 3.1's heading. Tests that a heading is indexed as content rather than skipped as structure.
Section 2.1's heading, on a different page from the other heading query, so a retriever pinned to one page of a paper fails here.
Section 4.1. From a paper whose body text arrives with words run together, so it exercises the opposite extraction shape from the Dijkstra queries.
Appears as section 4.5 on page 7 and again in the appendix on page 25. Recorded as both: a single expected page would be wrong.
Six occurrences across the paper. The broadest expectation in the set, and the one that would break a retriever that silently caps results per source.

The only unambiguous phrase in a math-heavy paper, and it is written space-free because that is how it sits in the extracted text. A query authored with spaces would find nothing here, which is the corpus's property and not the retriever's failure.
Section 5's heading, in the longest paper of the three.
Five occurrences across theory, method, related work and appendix. Together with the ARCS title query, the two cases where a per-source result cap would show.
First of eleven author affiliations on the title page. Unique to this paper.
ADR-0004 A12. A fabricated DOI must retrieve nothing. The string looks like an arXiv identifier and appears in no fixture.

ADR-0004 A12 again, in the shape a fabricated citation actually takes: a plausible title rather than a malformed identifier. A retriever that invented an excerpt here would pass every positive query above.

A term central to this project and absent from all three papers. Tests that the retriever reports absence rather than returning its nearest passage -- the failure that would let a citation cite whatever was closest.
Named in PHASE_1_WORKORDERS.md as a dependency the project must not have. Nothing in the corpus says it.

frozen.$comment: The empty query is a caller-level case, not a MATCH query: SQLite's FTS5 rejects an empty MATCH string as a syntax error. It belongs to the retrieval API's argument validation, not to this set, and is listed so it is not forgotten rather than tested here.

empty_string_query.why: ADR-0004 A6: an empty query is an absence, not an error and not a match-everything.
